Sunless sea is creepy, eerie and gloomy; but it is also very engaging. The stories told on each island is unique and will always have you coming back to see what's going on or seeing if you can alter your choices to get further along the story. An island of masks, a delivery for a shady character, spying on a foreign outpost, breaking into a prison, trading and building trust from multiple factions, becoming a mailman. These are all possible within the game.
Besides the island stories, you have your own story and goal to fulfill. You'll have to discover the map for yourself and plan your route while managing your fuel, supplies and terror as to not suffer the terrible fate of death, although there are many fates worse.
The game is a mashup of resource management and storytelling, which to be honest is a bit weird and off-putting to some. Travel is slow, which is therapeutic to some, aggravating to the impatient, or simply boring for most. My best advice is to play the game in a way that gives you the most enjoyment. If you're in it for the challenge of surviving, just play the game. If you're in it for the story, I'm sure you'll figure something out ;)
Keep in mind that this game has lots of reading. In fact, almost the whole game is reading. The beginning may be a bit daunting, but you'll come to soon understand the eerie, sunless world of the Unterzee.

I don't want to give this game a negative review, because the atmosphere and soundtrack are amazing, but there are just too many nitty-gritty details that get overlooked.
Pros:
-While not an original idea, the overall gameplay is definitely refreshing. From delving into complete darkness while using a light that may actually lure something monstrous your way, to infuriating yourself trying to get a decent haul, it's something entertaining.
- Interesting cast/backgrounds. While there isn't any character development or memorable characters, it's definitely nice to have some interesting characters tell you their fates.
Cons:
-It's something entertaining, but that comes at a huge thorn in your side. The "journal" is next to useless when it comes to remembering simple data, and all the quests are practially linear, if not even worth it to begin with.
-Lack of common sense with the rest of the world. Why do we never cross friendly ships that aid us in the game? Why are we only in control of one ship in this hell? Why are there no military forces from any countries in the story? (There are militant cities but it's odd that there isn't much control as their should be, given the back story)
-Nothing interesting ever happens. You might cross an eerie thing or two here and there, but it's mainly platonic. It's there every game, every time. It would be nice to see some variety.
-The reward system is horrible. Quests sometimes drain you more than they help.
-Very little development as far as forum feedback and Steam feedback is showing.
Overall, it's an honest 5/10.

I bought this game shortly after it came out on the 360 back in 2010... imagine the surprise that everyone had when they first played this game. We knew little about it, the art was simple, no soundtrack, and yet it surprised us in ways that very few games had before.
I would have dreams of walking in a dark forest, with the only source of light would be just beyond the pines, but it was still there. The forest would always be eeriely lifeless, nothing but the cold dirt underneath my feet, void of even the smallest insects, they don't exist yet. And yet, the only way to progress is to set trail in a world where nothing but you exist, however, a noise could be heard just beyond sight... a branch falling? Something falling? How about another person or thing?
In a world that only you exist, there lies another being, prodding it's way through the overgrowth, searching for another. Is it looking for a companion? or is it looking for prey? Either of which are frieghtening in it's own ways. But everything is silent once more, has it gone away? Or is it sitting silently hopeing to catch the sound of your own footsteps? Suddenly you become very quiet and self aware. Whatever it is that is out there...
it's coming closer.

I've never written a review for a game before. But then again, I've never felt so conflicted and annoyed by a game.
So much potential. And yet wasted. The writing and worldbuilding is excellent. Simply amazing. Not just Lovecraftian - somebody send China Mieville this game. He'll love it. I was consistently impressed with the ideas colonizing this world and the writing that effectively communicates them. The Khanate. The Demon Duchess. The Sisters of Hunter's Keep. Fantastic atmosphere.
And yet. What an incredibly frustrating game. Pretty soon it devolves into grinding and random transporting of objects from point to point. Combat is a joke. The hints of a greater story are tantalizing, but so opaque that you wonder if the writers have any real idea where it's headed.
But here's where it lost me. I was willing to waste 13 hours exploring and grinding, but then I randomly returned to port I found out that I had failed to deliver something (and I didn't know there was a time limit) and had upset someone. One random roll to see what happens.
I'm dead. That's it. 13 hours of grinding and slowly improving my ship and captain and I'm dead because I lost track of what I was supposed to deliver.
Wow. That's . . . . horrible design. Yeah, I could start over with another captain. I don't want to. In fact, the first thing I did was delete the game off my computer and vow never to play it again.
Permadeath games are fine, but when you make permadeath the result of one random roll in a dialogue tree . . . . yeah, no thanks.

I've played the game long enough now that I can give a basic review for the game. In terms of the knowledge progression I'm about 6% complete or so it says. I can say confidently enough that the game is interesting and has some decent mechanics that set it apart from similar games like Terraria and Starbound.
However, this game is very much a buggy mess right now and I would not say this is worthy to be called V1.0, it is very much still an early access game in my mind and if you are hoping to play this game without upset, I feel I need to tell you that you will be let down.
-Mining
Mining feels clunky at the best of times, it doesn't work like terraria or starbound where if you click on a tile then that tile gets removed, it's a directional thing and the mining tool isn't center with the playable characters model, it is off to the side a little and it makes mining a real chore.
-Monsters
The monster spawns are attrocious, they spawn anywhere even in the air, which makes falling down elevators you dig suicidal, it encourages the use of teleportation but really I find this a constricting mechanic and very poorly thought out by the developers. A fix that would make everyone happy in my opinion would be to limit mob spawns to front tiles or certain background tiles (such as dirt, clay etc)
-Monsters continued
Mobs can spawn in the air, regardless of the foreground or background tiles, I have confirmed this, and this doesn't only effect elevators and general exploration, mobs can spawn inside hangers you built for your vehicles, and those ships will die as the mob mindlessly floats back and forth rebounding off walls etc. This is completely ridiculous and wastes your resources needlessly.
-UI
The UI is a complete mess, it is extremely user unfriendly and lacks specific interactions like shift clicking to place items into recipe facility entities like the carbon refinery for example. You have to mouse them in one by one and when recipes require 5 items that are cluttered around your inventory, it is not fun to micromanage and makes organising inventory space and much more, a very annoying task.
-UI overlays
To add onto some of the UI problems the game has, the UI overlaps the screen in some instances, such as when "dominating" an area (or setting am item recipe as a task), the overlay that displays you have conquered the area acts as a none transparant pop up, basically it stops you from shooting or building while mousing over the overlay and this can lead to some pretty cheap deaths as I have experienced.
-Gameplay
The gameplay for the most part is fine, you progress at a steady pace and you are rewarded for killing monsters and mining generated tiles. However the dungeons you come across such as the zombie rooms seem to feel extremely off. You have to destroy 4 spawners and once that is complete, you have to plant 3 bombs, leave the chunk and then the entire land is just blown up. Any decoration blocks you might have wanted from the room are deleted, and you're left with an unappealing piece of land that does nothing. The game says you've "dominated" the land but you're just left with an ugly crater. Furthermore, you aren't rewarded in the slightest by blowing the chunk up, no EXP, no loot, nothing.
-SNAILS
HOLY ♥♥♥♥ING♥♥♥♥♥♥ SNAILS AND FROGS HAVE TO BE THE SINGLE MOST ANNOYING MECHANIC I HAVE EVER WITNESSED IN A VIDEO GAME. PLEASE NERF THEIR SPAWN RATE, IN FACT THAT BRINGS ME ONTO MY NEXT POINT
-Spawn rate
Monster spawn rate either seems to be so few or so disgustingly unbearable, the amount is completely random, you coulld be spelunking in a cave and come across one or two mud crabs, but then teleport back to base and an entire army of frogs, snails and crabs will rain from the sky.
-Frame rate
This is a really unfortunate aspect of the game, I have a really high end computer and I get frame lock ups quite often, it's not a long lock up but it is very common and happens in loaded chunks even if I am standing still. I don't have a clue what causes it and as far as I can tell from other reviews this seems to be a common problem.
-Rare crashes
The game as crashed a few times on me now. both times have happened when starting up a pregenerated world and entering a container too quickly. I am sure this will be fixed but it added to the frustration this game is to play right now.
-Instance glitches
In an instance you are similar in proprties to that of adventure mode in minecraft. You cannot place or remove blocks basically. If you happen to click too fast on a door (which is basically a teleporter to another part of the dungeon) yoiu can very easily be teleported out of bounds and you have to exit your game to fix the problem. The items needed to enter an instance dungeon aren't cheap so I find this to be a very harmful bug that impedes progression.
-Exploration
Now this may be due to the overall difficulty of the game, and I may be playing the game without fully understanding the metagame and what not, but I find exploration into the second biome (I think it's refered to as the comet biome, it's the ice themed one) to be extremely unforgiving. I have the weapons to deal with the monsters there in small numbers, but as I have said, as you fall down to lower levels, mobs spawn in the sky and can basically 1 hit ko you as you fall, but that's not the only problem, as you land on the surface of the main tier 2 biome, mobs that are faster than you are generated all around you, on the ground and in the sky and that makes exploration and progression an absolute chore. I have tried to find a way to set my spawn down there instead of on the first biome and I'm not sure how. The wiki for Edge of Space is extremely outdated and many pages are missing.
-Exploration continued
I have solved the issue of teleporting to lower levels, you have to build 2 command centres to teleport between areas. However now that I don't have to deal with the annoying elevator scenario, I have discovered that towards the lower half of the second biome, bears and penguins spawn in great abundance, regular bears can 2 shot you, and have more than doube the players moving speed so in tight spaces it is very hard to escape, they spawn almost everywhere in the cave systems down there and I simply cannot progress further below. I enjoy a hard game but I think something seems off with the spawn rate, they appear so frequently that I feel stunted to go any deeper. You might be thinking that I should gear up a little more before progressing, which is true, but all the radium I can find in the ice and all the illuminated crystals (that can drop radium) have been mined up in the top half of the biome. I made the mistake of building one of those NPC anchors with the radium (he was a useless NPC as well, did 100% nothing and that brings me onto my next point shortly) and now I lack the amount to create the desert armor set.
-NPC Anchors
I really like this idea, it's another resource sink and the potential for some really cool bonuses is there, but the developers really missed the mark on most of them. I believe Rob the robot is the most useful, fully upgraded he will drop Titanium ore for you occasionally, I have about a stack and a half of the stuff just sitting around and as Titanium is a pain to harvest, I like this NPC and my investment was worth it. However, NPCs such as Vinny (The potato plant) do nothing, regardless of the investment, his one ability is that every time you feed him 5 biomass and 5 ice, he will glow in the dark. That's ridiculous, I have lights everywhere, the investment and the space for his anchor completely outway his use. This is very similar for the other NPC's too, they could provide cool bonuses like 5% to sneak, or ore in a radius will glow, something that would actually be fun to invest these resources into. But nope, glow in the dark plants are apparently useful.
-Hit word limit, much more is broken-

Rushing up the hills of Iwo Jima.
Pop a frag grenade, cook it for 3 seconds, chuck it into the bunker, a jap torso comes flying out, only to be torched mid air by a flamethrower as we cook what was left of the bunker. Pushing up the hill again, jap bunkers and mg's all over, marines to my left and right dropping like flies, my squad gets behind a boulder. We hear that familiar screech, that of an incoming artillery shell, we get up and run for our lives, Those who dont make it far away enough, lose limbs and heads, those who do, get picked off out in the open. We keep pushing, taking gun positions, resisting enemy artillery, and occasional our own naval gunfire.
A jap rushes the bunker, 3 of them, bayonets out, clip empty, i rush towards them, stab one, pull out my m1911 and kill the rest. I chuck a smoke grenade, and a frag, and pick up a 30. cal, still on the bloody rock with the arm of its previous operator still attached. We rush the bunker, all 30 of us, dodging rounds left and right, jets of fire and smoke coming from both sides. I hip fire the 30. killing a jap that had his sights on me, and continue pushing.
I run outta 30., but a tommy gun is only a few feet away, this time the previous user a bit more intact than the last, i cant say the same for the guy next to him. I hit the bunker, throw a frag over the wall, and hear the screams, meaning its clear to move in. I enter the door, hit the wall, pump a few 45. acp rounds into it. A jet of fire shot through the narrow slit, as no one knew i was even in the bunker yet, torching me, luckily i survived. 11 rounds in the drum, another jap comes running in and i give him his just desserts.
I hear that scream, that scream for the emperor coming through the door, i dodge out of the way, reaching for my sidearm, i get it out, aim down the sights, *click*, he stabs me, i pop a frag, before he can re chamber his next round, and it goes off, killing him, and mortally wounding me even more. Im blacking out, starting to fade, as i peer out the narrow and charred slit of the bunker, hundreds of ships, landing craft, craters, and bodies, far too many to count.
The last thing i see is my fellow marines, charging the beach, most of them getting ripped apart by artillery, or stripped of their life by a sharp shooters bullet.
If their is one piece of advice i can give to any player, who ever dares to play this game.
Never, Stop, Running.

Though very intrigued and excited for the unique gameplay this title was boasting, I grew hesitant to purchase SUPERHOT at full price once I caught wind of its very short campaign. Convinced I would not enjoy playing challenge modes enough to justify the cost, I held off for a couple weeks. However, my desire to actually play with the mechanics that had peaked my interest in the first place won out and I found myself emptying my Steam wallet.
Contrary to my presumptions, I thoroughly enjoy the various modes this game has to offer, with plans on playing them periodically till the day I feel the icy grip of Death around me. Where the real payoff lain, though, was in the compaign, brief as it is. While I unabashedly indulge in AAA titles, I found myself more fulfilled by the one or two hours it took to complete the story mode of SUPERHOT, due to its uniqueness, and felt I had gotten my money's worth.
If one enjoys classic sci-fi stories that breach the fringe of reality and implicitly ask philosophical questions, then this game is worth your time for the story alone. Beyond that, hours of entertainment can easily be achieved in the other game modes, most notably the Endless Mode.

Exactly what it says on the tin: a Telltale plot-driven game with Batman. That's a significant distinction from it being a Batman game made by Telltale, as you'll see.
Now usually i review games by listing their pros and cons in my opinion. This time i won't, because my feelings towards this game are markedly negative and a traditional wall of text serves them better. So, let's get this out of the way immediately: this game is more action packed than your average Telltale episodic game, but everything is still all about completing some ludicrously easy quick time events and watching the action stiffly unfold while the antiquated engine struggles to handle some decent combat animations. This is not a game that you'll buy for the awesome Batman fighting antics, but they did a good job at nailing the atmosphere, some of the costumes and most character designs, so it'll still feel like you're in a Batman game at the very least. That being said, and knowing that your choices in this game have as much of a modest impact on the grand scheme of things as ever, I suppose you'll buy this game for its plot. Now, the plot of this series isn't inherently bad. It's a decent, if rather standard, criminal intrigue for the first few episodes and then ups the ante later on by introducing the main villain far too late. What really could or could not hinder your enjoyment of this game, if you buy it knowing all the classic Telltale crap that awaits you (plus a copious amount of poor clipping, terrible animation errors and unjustified frame rate drops that make these games feel REALLY rushed out), is your opinion on the plot and characterization. Without spoiling anything, it can be seen as either a fresh take on classic characters and plotlines that will keep even die-hard Batfans wondering what'll happen next, or a butchering of the established canon surmounted by characters being and acting nothing like their usual selves. I saw it as the latter, sadly, thus these were for me 5 frustrating episodes where nothing was sacred. It was like the Gotham TV series in terms of disregarding canon and reinventing famous characters, but in my opinion this series tried too hard to be edgy and different from the usual Batman canon, and didn't deliver a convincing alternative. Characterization is either dull, bluntly idiotic or a mixture of both, with Batman himself being one of the worst offenders and Harvey Dent's temper tantrums being a mixed bag but still some of the most convincing writing in the entire series, and that says a lot. I can stop a moment and say that renowned voice actors like Troy Baker and Dave Fennoy managed to somehow sound wooden, monotone and terribly uninterested throughout the whole series, which was really heartbreaking, but the point is this game can only be good if the plot is, since everything else is rough, basic or non-existent. For me, this game had a terrible plot and an unsatisfying conclusion with the obvious cliffhanger ready for Season 2, because god forbid Telltale from not milking dry whatever license they can get their hands on. That said, this is a personal review and there will certainly be many ferociously disagreeing with me. I do not recommend this game, especially not to Batman fans. As a sidenote, this game was a gift from a friend, so my opinion is untarnished by money matters.

The forest would always be eeriely lifeless, nothing but the cold dirt underneath my feet, void of even the smallest insects, they don't exist yet. And yet, the only way to progress is to set trail in a world where nothing but you exist, however, a noise could be heard just beyond sight... a branch falling? Something falling? How about another person or thing?
In a world that only you exist, there lies another being, prodding it's way through the overgrowth, searching for another. Is it looking for a companion? or is it looking for prey? Either of which are frieghtening in it's own ways. But everything is silent once more, has it gone away? Or is it sitting silently hopeing to catch the sound of your own footsteps? tl;dr — Text-based story (think FTL), slow-burn, requires patience. Good game. Bad Price. Buy only at a significant discount.
As a fan of Echo Bazaar/Fallen London, I enjoyed the premise of the game. However, it's precisely because that other game exists that I can't recommend this one. Too much of the experience is already available for free to merit spending $20 or $30 on this game.
Pros:
· Lore-heavy — (if you enjoy that), but not stifling to the point where you need to be immersed in the lore to enjoy gameplay (for the rest of us)
· Explore the world of Fallen London in a familiar format — In other words, go play Fallen London first. It's free. If you like it, then consider this.
· Genuinely harrowing sea-monster encounters — A different person might call them unfair, but as you see from this list...
· Brutal survival mechanics — I'm a fan of the genre, and enjoy the challenge, but it takes a certain amount of patience.
· Optional permadeath/save mechanic — Sometimes there are honest mistakes you want to undo. Moving on from one captain to the next is an important in-game mechanic, though.
Cons:
· Extremely slow start — I didn't feel like I was making any progress until my fourth captain.
· No clear direction — Without an online guide, it's nearly impossible to tell what is and is not profitable until you do it.
· RNG-heavy — Much of your success is based on the encounters you have at different ports. Skill and planning are important, but nothing beats luck for a good start.
· Lore-saturated — While I said above that the lore did a lot for world-building and is not strictly necessary to enjoy the gameplay, the lore is still incredibly dense and is rarely explained plainly. You are expected to fumble about until you start to understand things.
For future reference, as of this review, the prices are $18.99 for Sunless Sea, and $29.98 for a bundle with Zubmariner. Zubmariner on its own is $10.99

Outlast is a virtual experience where the story's fabrications induce suspense, haunting horrors, and jump scares. Although, the direction in which the story develops, followed by simple repetitive objectives undermines the greatness this horror game has to offer.
During my 6-hour walkthrough of the main game, the majority of the time, I was screaming or quietly panicking at what could be around the corner, just waiting for me. Whether it was the pure gore, lore-rich journals and notes, or the insane patients within the asylum looking to kill me. Outlast stays true to the horror genre, and like the game’s protagonist, keeps me wanting to find the exit from this insane world the game creates. Furthermore, with fine details such as the bloody footprints your character leaves and being able to see your own body, help with the illusion that you are in the game. However, about 4 hours into the game, or 3 chapters of the story, a majority of devices used to trick the player into feeling directly involved lose this effect. A key component that causes the player to disassociate with Outlast’s story are the continuous story objectives. Whether it be turning valves or finding a key, these objectives bog down the momentum of the player’s escape and make the game feel like a forced tour of the Mount Massive Asylum. Lastly, Outlast’s decision to focus in on the sci-fi components of the lore and ending of the story, creates a confusing and subpar explanation to why the experimentation within the asylum occur.
Despite the elements that underwhelm story development and gameplay, Outlast does a great job at being a horror game. So if you’re looking for something to scare ya, and are not too worried about the game’s story, Outlast is a good game to play.

There is no casual train management strategy game quite like Train Valley.  Explore new worlds and learn the rail management skills to build, manage, and rule your great rail empire.  No train enthusiast on a budget can go without this game. There are a few kinks (i.e. buildings spawning on laid tracks and trains spontaeously exploding for no reason) but they are so rare or predicatable you can adapt to your situation.  I am proud to say I had the privelege to enjoy this game from early developement, and you can witness that experience for yourself in my let's play from the earliest alpha release to the most recent patch (a7.4/beta1.0 at this period) here:
I personally want to thank
and Oroboro Games for the fantastic experience they provided me and cannot wait for the next patch.  There is so much more to experience!
Advice for new users:
-the bell, whistle or horn sound a locomotive makes leaving a station in this patch gives you a cue of how fast it will go regardless of what it looks like (mid or late 19th century steam, 20th century steam, early diesel, modern diesel)
-the grid matrix in build mode is your friend; drag your cursor from a place that has track wherever you want, just be sure you are aware of how you drag your mouse cursor
-dirt roads on game maps give you a hint about how to configure your tracks
-compact triangular swicthing junctions are essential for saving money and space, crosing tracks are not
-plot your track configuations while the game is paused to be safe (or don't for an extra challenge) :3
-train crashes require track replacement at the point of impact (unless the impact point is in a station)
-don't leave a train sitting in a station sitting for too long; it will eventually leave
-consider in game annual taxes paid each new year before building or adding more trains (which both cost money)
-trains going into the wrong station will go straight in and swing back out instantly, so be careful
-avoid building over existing map strutures to save more money where reasonable
-game logic prevents trains from derailling on switches regardless of which way they are oriented
-building new tracks under existin tracks with trains still running on them will cause derailments (game logic won't save you here)
-enjoy yourself
P.S. (Please don't throw rocks at me for sounding like a brown-noser, I just like this game a lot.)

I was in the battlefield, proudly serving the Third Reich, defending our rightfully earned teritory from the Russian dogs. I was killing Russian after Russian, with Das Deutschlandlied blaring in the background. A Russian peeks his head out of the trench in front of me, and stares me down. I stare at him back, and he ducks. I toss my Stick of Germany Glory, or what you like the call a 'grenade' in the trench, and he pops back out and shoots me. I lie there, dying, but a smile on my face. I look at him one last time, and utter my last words, "All hail Deutschland." He blows up, body in the air, and I lie there in glory of the battlefield.
EDIT: Might as well make this a real review.
So first off, I got this game since a couple of my friends played this so I thought "Why not, let's see why     they love this so much." This is no regular, main stream WWII game just like Call of Duty. If you're looking for a game like that, just walk away man. Just walk away. Red Orchestra 2 features a game mode, popular by the community, called Territory/Realism. It's basically a campaign between the Axis (Nazis) and Allies (Red Army/Russians) where you fight for territories across Russia into Stalingrad, hence the name, Heroes of Stalingrad. The realism part is self explanitory. Bullet drop, one shot kills (with bolt action rifles), etc. I always play this mode whenever I'm on, although, a lot of good servers for Terrioty/Realism are full, it's worth finding a good match. This also includes Rising Storm, which is basically the same thing except it's in the Pacific, where it's Japanese vs United States. Offering new maps, it also gives a larger variety of weapons. The United States are given the flamethrower (or as I prefer to call it by its origional German name, fammenwafer). I don't really need to explain that, do I? The Japanese Squad Leaders and Team Leaders spawn with a katana. That's right, a ♥♥♥♥ing katana. With that, they could 'bonzai', which is charging the enemy head on, katana out and ready to kill some dishonerabu Americans (just a joke... don't get butthurt) and now has pretty much became the official Japanese tactic against Americans.
TL;DR ---  In all honesty, I ♥♥♥♥ing love this game. If you want a challenging, realistic WWII game, this is for you.
11/10, would serve the Third Reich again.

I wanna preface this by saying I'm a big fan of narrative/choice-driven stories and Telltale in particular. I have played several of their games and often suggest my friends do the same.
I really didn't care about this game. To me, this story fell short of many things, but mainly, being interesting. Telltale games usually hook me right away, but after three episodes, I still wasn't dedicated enough to the characters or story to wanna keep playing. Maybe I'm just tired of visiting and revisiting Bruce's bummer backstory and inability to cope with his guilt complex. Or maybe I just don't care about stories that aren't, I don't know, compelling?
I really enjoyed the voice actors (Travis Willingham especially) but as Telltale only has like five I could have played any other game and had a better time with it. The story felt formulaic, though I guess there were a couple of twists I didn't see coming and I thought Harvey Dent's storyline was well done. I also appreciated what they were trying to do with the crime scene puzzles/fight choreography stuff but I dunno, it felt like more of the same: uninteresting.
I'm also getting really sick of my choices not actually making a difference. Especially when this is pretty much Telltale's biggest selling point.
I considered begrudgingly recommending this game. Then I realized I literally forget about it when I tell people to play Telltale games in real life, so no, I won't be recommending it here, either.

This game is fun, however.. not finished.
I've already had alot of fun with the game,
Let me start with saying that this is my first Tropico game.
I'll state my opinion on the positive and negative aspects below:
Positive:
Humor:
This game has a great sense of humor, everytime you research something you'll get your general reporting to you in a somewhat.. weird form. It can certainly provide you with a laugh from time to time.
Campaign:
I still haven't got far due to the invasions and rebels, but i've already notices that there is a variety of missions to play.
You can even pick one of the two islands which you are going to play a certain mission on.
Quests:
Lots of quests and tasks, there is always a goal for you.
Negative:
Military
The first thing i noticed, and which also became my downfall and got me quite angry with the game.. is the military(war) system. You build military posts which exist out of one squad of soldiers. Can you control them? No! During invasions or rebel events you cannot control your forces. Even if it's 10 squads against five you will probably still lose due to the horrible path-finding system. You cannot control your squad. They go to a certain building and will not engage with any enemy troops on the way. Mostly the squads will just walk around aimlessy, not defending anything.. while your building are being burned down. For instance, one squad gets to the enemy and gets into a fight.. they'll get slaughtered because it'll most likely be 5 squads versus 1.  And that's basically how i lost all the time. Not to mention that the rebels are quite overpowered.
Trading & Items
I am quite disappointed with this, In the beginning i had the idea i could control my economy. But there isn't even a storage building where your people bring the goods to, they just ship off at regular prices automatically. You can browse the trade offers manually and send one of your own ships to buy or sell products, however. But yet no actual gather and build system, that's a big thing that's just missing..
Alive atmosphere.
I am missing the Stronghold idea.
What i mean with this is basically i'm missing to see my country workers actually work, going to the taverns, church, free time spendations.. etc soldiers patrolling the streets, vehicles picking up goods and the delivering them to a certain location(A to B),  more depth in the building constructions carryíng planks and goods and hammeríng, sawíng buildings together. That's one big thing that's missing for me.
Sad'ly there is more negativity in my mind than positive, thus the reason i marked my review as negative.
However it's still a fun game, but i do not agree with the 50,00 euro's we're getting charged.
In-Fact, I had a update today.. a minor updates but no 'new' things. I doubt they'll ever be coming. There are still DLC'S coming along the way.
If you want to fill as if you are in a Michael Bay movie Get this game.

This game has come a long way since when it started in Early Access.  It is now the first 1.0 'Official Release'as of last week.  I'm a thumbs up but if you read my full review you'll see below what can be impoved on as well.
I've stuck with this game and I still enjoy it.  It is a crafting, exploring game in 2D... but it's in space!  And if you like space games that are open world and exploritory, I think you'll find this one not to like.  The are lots of materials to search for, interesting knowledge tree to work towards for crafting new gadgets and gizmos, and plenty of creepy monsters and weird vegetation to learn about.  So if you like figuring out the unknown, you'll like this.  It's kinda like Terraria, Metroid, and Star Trek blended together, with a dash of Avatar but something kinda unique too.
The Edge of Space development team says they will keep improving this game post release and I hope they do.
3 things which need some immediate attention by the development team include:
-  The game engine processes data and movement too slowly compared to other games in this genre.  The result is that movement is slow and battle can be clunky for game play.  I don't think this is my processors' or video card's fault as I play similiar games with even better graphics and gameplay, without so much latency.  Maybe the coding could be tighter / more real time.  Seems like a lot of processor overhead going on.
- The opening movie is pretty untelling still.  It's better now that it's 1.0 but this is supposed to be the intro to the adventure.  The user doesn't get a good sense of what the background story is and where they fit in.  And what's with the other 3 organizations with different symbols?  Are they competitors or allies?  Are they the Ark Corp council?  Are they the ones who blew up our ship or was it an alien war?  It's hard to tell and it shouldn't be.
-  The addition of Fineous the Shark has helped teach new players (and older ones) what the controls and game mechanics are.  It could be a little more obvious though.  Probably the best way is to make sure the Codex has more content and the user knows right away that this is their one stop shop for learning about their new world, and how and what an agent of Ark Corp is supposed to do and try to acheive.  Some more work on the goals of the game are needed.  The Codex should be like our 'Hitchhikers Guild to the Galaxy'; everything you need to know when you thunk on a new planet in a Cryopod without any friends or contact with where you blasted off from, after a long cryo-frozen nap. I like the sense of humour though so far; keep that going.
That's my thoughts on this game so far.  I recommend, as long as you don't expect perfection just yet but I think it's worth supporting and playing.  It's fun and interesting to explore.
This Review was written Sept. 20, 2015.

Ok, i admitt, i haven't played thet game for a long time before i started writting this review. I know, it's wrong, but after time i spent in-game, i can hazard a guess that i saw everything The Expendabros has to offer.
The Expendabros is 2D action platformer. As store page says, it's some kind of variation about "THE EXPENDABLES 3". Your goal? Get from left side of the map to right side, free your "bros" and kill the bad guys. In as bloody way as you can.  Simple. Game looks like typical Hollywood war movie: pumped up hero moves through countless enemy soldiers, destroying everything he can. And you know what? Even if it sounds boring and pathetic,
Especially when mixed with fully destroyable environment, tones of explosive barrels (2 types, one just blows up, and second flies up into the sky, destroying everything on it's way) and saws.
Heroes. Game allows us to play as one of seven characters, based on movie series. How are they diffrent? Apart of looks? Weapons. While game gives us three types of attacks (promary, special, wchih needs to be reffiled with ocassional ammo, and of course, meele), all characters attack in diffrent way. So, one rushes with two guns and sticky grenades as special, other throws cloud of knifes, or plays knife artillery, throwing them into air, another shoots with shotgun filled with incendiary ammo, and throws incendiary grenade. And thoose are only three characters. Every attack (excluding meele, same for every character) destroys place. Map gets torn apart by us, enemies, explosives, so after our game, it looks worse than worlds economy.  All of this to see comical "area liberated" after victory.
While playing, you encounter guys walking around (thay can be armed to help you) and cages. Player has to destroy cage and free his bro. Freeing enough of them unlocks new character. Maybe it sounds nice, seeing al characters and choosing one, your favourite to play with, but no.
There's no way (or maybe i just didn't found one) to pick your favourite muscle, and how often do they change? Well, random one at the beggining of the round, randon change after freeing prisoner, and random one after death. We should be hurry to love our heros because they are gone so fast. Other thing that bugs me are controls on keyboard. I played on WASD, so fight keys are TYU. Claustrophobical, isn't it? Even though you can change controls, a) i think that developers should make a good default settings, to make game good for begginers; b) settings are aviable only in main menu. You can't change them after starting game. And you have to just look at them before play, because there's no tutorial. If you want to play, you have to figure everything out by yourself. Maybe it's better on the controller (full supported). Want to play with friends? Local Coop only. Still better that no multiplayer mode at all, right?
Even though problems listed above, i think this game is woth giving it a go. Especially, it's free to download untill December. Unless you are tired of american pathriotism, american flag, and american movies.

First off, I highly recommend this game. It's unique.
Note that the creators of the game, did not give a clear answer to what really happened to that boy and his sister and they wanted us to make our own theories about it. There are a lot of theories and we cannot take one of them as the correct one. Here's what I believe.
Let's begin from the title. Limbo. That's a place where, based on some religions, after people die in real life, their souls go there for an unspecific period of time until God judge them and decide if they deserve to go into heaven or hell. So, by the time that the boy is in the limbo, we clearly understand that
.
As the game begins, he wakes up in the middle of a forest looking for her sister. The reason why he is doing that, is because he doesn't understand that he's dead and he believes that he has lost her sister, so she's searching for her. We don't know how he died, but it's possible that he fell from their treehouse because his sister is kneeling in the last scene and there's a rope ladder besides her. Each area of the game represents his life. Starts off in a mysterious forest with spiders being his fear that he tries to overcome. Next "level" is the school life with other kids who were bullying the homeless guy. He then had a traveling job, traveling and living in motels and
s and getting to new places and he eventually end up working in a factory. I also believe that the light worms that stick to his head represent the community who wants to control his brain and make him unable to reach his final destination. You continue the game passing through many obstacles just like you do in real life before you reach your purpose.
In the end, he eventually
and sees her kneeling. The scene is not clear enough, but I believe that she was crying about his death and praying for him. Her sister doesn't turn around to greet him but she feels the presence of his soul and that's why she somehow gets upset. In that moment, the boy finds out that he's dead as he approaches his sister and the game ends abruptly.
As I already said, there are a lot of theories that we can imagine and seem to "fit", but we don't really know what happened. That's all I believe, even if my theory has some flaws (didn't mention the Glass part).

I'm going to give Morphopolis a lukewarm recommendation, because the artwork is gorgeous, and I'm a sucker for both point-and-click adventures and games with a unique visual style.  If those things sound up your alley, then definitely give Morphopolis a try.  I do have reservations though, as the game can become very tedious, as it basically consists of navigating very slow-moving insects between various screens as you look for hidden objects, and solving small puzzles.  The controls are also frustrating at times.  There are five segments to play through, but there is no real ending once you've completed the final puzzle.  Speaking of the final puzzle, it almost caused the game to lose my recommendation, as it is basically an annoying slider puzzle, and I really can't stand when these show up in games.  All of that being said, however, Morphopolis remains a beautiful, relaxing experience, and it's likely worth your time.

Evolve (just played the alpha) is the highly looking forward title from a team of Left4Dead makers and at least the publisher of Borderlands (Take2). Long time it has existed as a draft for a superior type of Co-op shooter in a new universum of darkness and danger.
So some elements felt like pretty familiar from the first moment. Like matchmaking and the well balanced team co-oping of 4 different characters. (Medic, Assault, Trapper and Support). It is instead highly possible there is a team hunter wipeout or a monster death before.
The game world is pretty dark and vivent. It's recommended to not attack every creature you see if you mustn't. The maps are quite small but otherwise still kiteable by the monster. The 3D models are high detailed and unique dues to the CryEngine takes all power into the rendering. A nice idea is to show the game progress after every match with symbolized colored dots running over the minimap like little sperms. Also the glowing monster tracks for the hunters and the sniffing mode of the monster are very useful.
Altogether I can say the game looks and feels fantastic. But it still has potential to evolve even more as a common co-op blockbuster. Hopefully there can be done something about the graphics performance during the beta phase. I miss also somekind of really cool quotes ...

You want some action? Come get some! This sneak peek weekend showed what the game is about and how far they are with the development. Goliath weekend with good 1v4 gaming action.
Basicly its just about an evolving monster engaging on humans and a spec-ops-team trying to get down the monster.
Playing as a monster or as a member of the spec-force, both can be hard to play, depending on the map. The main objective for the monster is to eat little monsters and evolve to get stronger to get down the hunters or the power relay. The Hunters try to kill the monster by chasing it. As the monster is obviously faster then the Hunters they should try to place traps (mines/hooks) at keypoints on the map and lead it into the direction of it. On other maps there is also the opportunity to intercept it. Also monster can climb almost anywhere but  a hunter has to use the jetpack wisely to follow. None should try to face the monster alone. Every hunterclass is inportant for the team to win.
Nice animations of the environment, little monsters and creatures also with a great flora. Didn't saw any major graphic bug. Sometimes if you hit a mine and you were jumping you fly up to the roof of the trees. Couldn't test on highest settings cause of my machine limitation - tested on medium settings with no tessellation.
As a hunter I had problems following the monster cause it was so hilly and the jetpack runs out very fast. Cause I played the Monster very often it was easy just to jump down somewhere and climb up after they followed. They are stucked there then for like 20 seconds - if jetpack is empty.
It's a very team-based game - if you play as a hunter of course. So if there is one weak hunter, that can turn into a losing fight very easily. Arenas are not always "healthy" for the hunters. The Monster can sneak away easy if there are no traps or hooks. There should somehow be a Stage 2 fight before the Monster can get to Stage 3 and be able to shut down they relay fully powered.
Kraken's abilitys are obviously to strong. I've killed a level 8 team on Stage 1.
Now that was the "Alpha" of the game. Sort of a big Promotion of the game, testing the servers and see what size and form of maps give results to the game, I think. I dont go on balancing issues. Hopefully they take some time for the maps and give out some more on release. With an average of 12 minutes gameplay its ok for fast action.
Since I can just find DLC informations about new hunters and monsters I can't say there is big amount of long term excitement. They should tell if they plan multiple game modes. With that graphical design and ambiance they definitely can do more out of the game. But I expect they'll have stable servers on release.
Overall I confirm this is a nice game already, with good potential to be more than a 1 mode game.
Hope this review is useful for you folks :)

Here is my 'First Day on Launch Day!" Early Access Review Video:

To watch my early access review, please simply search "Zaxtor99 Train Valley" on Youtube.  Once Steam YouTube links are correctly working again, I will post the actual link here}
Pretty fun and challenging little train game, works very well for an early access game and I can't wait to watch this game progress towards completion.
Don't confuse this game with much more sandbox train simulation games like Sid Meier's Railroad, or it will likely leave you disappointed.  But for a simple little puzzle and management type of game, this game succeeds very well, especially for such an early access state.
I like it so far, and here are my early access launch day scores:
- VALUE (worth 40 points):  At $9.99, this game offers a pretty good value for the money with plenty of challenge.  30/40
- FUN (worth 30 points): The Fun factor is definitely here, and where this game shines.  Trying to manage the trains, the   tracks and your money and income on each progressively more difficult level is loads of fun.  25/30.
- CONTROLS & BUGS (worth 20 points):  The controls are simple and easy to figure out, and this is nice allowing you to focus on the mission objectives, track switches, and everything else that is part of this game.  No bugs I've seen.  20/20.
- GRAPHICS & SOUND (worth 10 points):  The graphics and sound are plenty nice for this kind of game.  8/10.
TOTAL SCORE: 30 + 25 + 20 + 8 = 83%.  My early access review for this game is an 83%.  Like I said above, I like this game and this pretty high score comes from the game offering a lot of value and fun and solid controls with no bugs found in me first day in early access experience to this point.  Not a bad score for an early access game!  :-)
